title: Operationalizing the Potential for Growth of Political Parties in a Multiparty System
section: Funnel of Causality, adaptation to the Quebec context
text:
Funnel of Causality, adaptation to the Quebec context


Model developed in the American two-party context, 20th century
Less strong party identification in Canada (Jenson 1975)
Considerable influence of short-term factors on Canadian voters (Blais 2004, Kilibarda et al. 2020)
Heterogeneity of salience, micro-publics (Krosnick 1990), hybrid media system
Therefore.. considerable room for maneuver



obviously, it needs to be adapted heterogeneity: fragmentation of issue salience and reception channels, especially in the context of social networks, must be considered in the issues/candidates block postulate: room for maneuver > than what classical theories suggest

title: Operationalizing the Potential for Growth of Political Parties in a Multiparty System
section: Theorizing the Potential for Growth: Two Distinct Concepts
text:
Theorizing the Potential for Growth: Two Distinct Concepts

Static potential for growth: by maintaining its current positions on an issue.Achieved through political communication strategies.
Dynamic potential for growth: by adopting the optimal set of positions on issues.Assumes that the static potential for growth is achieved.


Political communication: strategy on social networks, better targeting different segments, highlighting certain messages, etc.

Better suited to multiparty systems

Distinguishes between unattainable and attainable voters → potential for growth

text:

this graph shows the predicted RCI for challengers among CAQ voters at each RCI level for the CAQ we clearly see that, on the individual level, PQ was the party that would benefit from caq decline

title: Operationalizing the Potential for Growth of Political Parties in a Multiparty System
section: Estimated Distribution of Negative RCI Across the 125 Ridings
text:
Estimated Distribution of Negative RCI Across the 125 Ridings


Here we see the distribution of ridings according to their estimated potential for growth for each party Estimation based on linear models projected on post-stratification tables Models only made on non-voters of the parties, negative IRC We can see that the PQ has the highest potential for growth among the challenger parties Interesting fact: the CAQ has the highest potential for growth: could the CAQ have won even more? This supports the idea that the rise of the PQ is more due to the decline of the CAQ, which was in a good position But assuming the CAQ was going to fall, why the PQ?

title: Operationalizing the Potential for Growth of Political Parties in a Multiparty System
section: Potential for Growth of Challengers in Constituencies Won by the CAQ
text:
Potential for Growth of Challengers in Constituencies Won by the CAQ


This graph presents the potential for growth on the left and the vote share in the 2022 election of the challenger parties in constituencies won by the CAQ If we only consider the vote share on the right, the four parties seem in a good position, especially the PCQ In the graph on the left, we see that the PQ was the challenger with the highest potential for growth in CAQ constituencies

title: Operationalizing the Potential for Growth of Political Parties in a Multiparty System
section: Next Steps
text:
Next Steps
Final objective: systematic model that identifies electoral segments to target (static) and optimal positioning (dynamic)


More developed theoretical framework

Spatial theory of voting

Data from the VPL electoral compass

Allows testing of multiple issues in the same model
Issue salience

Survey experiments → associate the IRC with probabilities, perform simulations based on surveys
Dynamic potential for growth: systematize, simulations, machine learning, etc.



Spatial theory of voting: taking the position of other parties on the issue Machine learning: complex problem with multiple dimensions, necessity for simulations etc. The models are not necessarily complex (linear regressions with classic IVs or SEM), but the simulation is more complex Combinatorial optimization
